svg.text: Drive: 4WD, diff lock, tray, power steering
Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'drive'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: D03: PICO.GP9 -> BTS1.EN - R_EN and L_EN joined
D06: BTS1.M+ -> ACT_DIFF.M+ - Wrong way? Change DIFF_LOCK_DIR in firmware, not the wires
D08: ADS1.VDD -> ACT_DIFF.POT_HI - Pot on 3.3 V, never 12 V
D28: BAT12.pos -> ADS1.A1 - an.aux_12v. Fuse the sense lead
D29: PI_BUCK.VOUT -> BRAKE_PEDAL.V5 - Or the Pico buck. 5 V sensor
D30: BRAKE_PEDAL.SIG -> ADS2.A0 - an.brake_pedal, 4.5 V reads 3.0 V
D31: RAIL.BUS -> RELAYS2.COM1 - Steering ignition feed through relay 9, so the lock and RC kill can turn assist off
D33: EPS_ECU.MOTOR -> EPS_COL.MOTOR - Toyota's own plug, keep it from the wrecker
PICO: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 - Talks to the Pi over CAN only. No USB lead to the Pi; reflash with a laptop on its own USB port in the workshop
BRAKE_PEDAL: Brake pedal Hall sensor - Brake regen only, once the Shinegle check passes
RAIL: Dash 12 V rail - Key OR relay 8 (power hold). Stays up after key-off until the Pico lets go
ADS2: Second ADS1115 (0x49) - Brake pedal regen only
RELAYS2: 16-ch relay board, channels 9-16 (2 used, 6 spare) - Same board as RELAYS. Relay 9 steering enable, relay 10 drive lock (uses the NC contact)
PI_BUCK: Pololu D36V50F5 5 V 5.5 A - Pi 5 power. About 16 W of its 27 W with the AI HAT+ 2 fitted
ACT_DIFF: Front diff lock actuator (50 mm, pot)

FB: Blade fuse block - 12 fuses in use. Small loads that can go out together share a fuse (front bars in pairs, trailer tail + stop, interior bar + accessory). All four front bars are NOT on one fuse, so one fault can't black out the front at night. The winch, control box power, key, power hold and each actuator keep their own. A 20-way leaves 8 spares
ACT_4WD: 2WD/4WD actuator - 50 mm actuator, or drive the stock Kawasaki electric 4WD actuator instead
ADS1: ADS1115 ADC (0x48) - ALERT pin left free so GP22 can be the steering CAN chip select (read "ready" over I2C)
BRAKE_PRESS: Brake line pressure sensor - Optional cross-check for the pedal sensor, 0.5-4.5 V
EPS_ECU: Toyota Aqua EPS ECU (89650-52B51) - Wrecker column, bench test with the Prius CAN frames first. ECU plug pinout TBC
BAT12: 12 V aux battery - Kept after the conversion. Charged by the DC-DC
EPS_COL: Aqua steering column (motor + torque sensor) - Motor and torque sensor plugs go to the ECU on Toyota's own loom

svg.text: D28 0.5 mm² 1 A via divider 10k / 2.2k + 3.3 V zener
